name: Sultan Aji Muhammad Sulaiman Sepinggan International Airport
before:
The main airport for Balikpapan and the largest in East Kalimantan, on the Indonesian side of Borneo. It flies domestically to Jakarta, Surabaya and Denpasar, and internationally to Singapore, Malaysia and Brunei.

Its importance is about to grow. The airport is set to become one of the main gateways to Nusantara, Indonesia's new capital city, connected to it by a toll road.

The terminal is a good one. Opened in September 2014 and covering 110,000 square metres, it was built for 10 million passengers a year to replace an old building rated for just 1.7 million that was handling 7.1 million. It is branded an eco-airport, with a water recycling plant and energy efficient air conditioning, and has 11 jet bridges, 74 check-in counters and 8 baggage carousels. Airports Council International named it the second best airport in the world for service quality in its size band in 2018.

One thing to warn a nervous flyer about: the single runway extends into a densely built up area, and landings here are often described as dramatic and demanding.

It is still widely called Sepinggan Airport.
after:
The main airport for Balikpapan and East Kalimantan. Flights run to Jakarta, Surabaya and Denpasar. International flights go to Singapore and Kuala Lumpur.

The airport puts its growing traffic down to Balikpapan's place as the main way into Nusantara, the new capital being built in East Kalimantan.

Its terminal dates from 2014, built for 10 million passengers a year to replace an old building rated for just 1.7 million that handled 7.1 million in 2013. Designed as an eco-airport, it opened with 11 jet bridges, 74 check-in counters and 8 baggage carousels. Airports Council International placed it second in the world for service among airports handling 5 to 15 million passengers a year, in awards for 2017 presented in 2018.

It is still widely called Sepinggan Airport.

claims.claim: ACI named it second best for service quality in its size band in 2018
claims.wasBefore: Airports Council International named it the second best airport in the world for service quality in its size band in 2018.
claims.why: Reworded: the award was ACI's Airport Service Quality Awards 2017, presented in September 2018 (Republika). Kept (see above).

claims.claim: the single runway extends into a densely built up area; landings dramatic and demanding
claims.wasBefore: One thing to warn a nervous flyer about: the single runway extends into a densely built up area, and landings here are often described as dramatic and demanding.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. Its source, the East Kalimantan transport office's page 'Bandara Sepinggan dikepung rumah', now answers 404 and its archived copy is in the web archive, which the network policy blocks. The single runway itself is confirmed (the regulator lists one, 2,500 by 45 m; OurAirports lists one) but on its own is not worth a sentence.

quote: Runways listed: 1

sources.quote: Due to its single runway extending into a densely built-up area, landings at the airport are often described as both visually dramatic and technically challenging for pilots.

claims.claim: first-half 2026 traffic: 2,392,873 passengers
claims.why: Held back: the airport's own release of 10 July 2026 gives 2,392,873 passengers, 21,789 aircraft movements and about 23,847 tonnes of cargo for January to June 2026. The old text gives no current passenger figure (its 7.1 million is the 2013 history of the terminal), so this replaces nothing; it would go in as an attributed figure if Andy wants one. No full-year 2025 total could be read: Statistics Indonesia refused the Surabaya helper's requests, and the regulator's 'Lalu Lintas Udara (2025)' count on the airport page (2,884,602) is not a full-year total.
